articleBlocks: Band and Chain can feel like they belong to music or linked objects instead of tools, which is why the board takes a moment to settle. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Coping gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Hack points toward equipment, but it still might not be enough if you are thinking about metaphors like hacks or chains.
Coping is the clue that makes the workshop answer clear.
Coping saw is too specific to ignore, and once saw clicks, band saw, chainsaw, hacksaw, and jigsaw all fall into place.
The answer was Types of saws.
This board is a good example of how one specialized clue can organize a list of more familiar words.
solutionNarrative: Band and Chain felt broad enough to belong almost anywhere, and Hack only partially pushed the board toward tools. The clues were fair, but they needed one more specialized term to settle.
Coping provided that term. Once coping saw came to mind, the rest of the board reorganized into familiar saw names instead of a pile of ambiguous short words.

lessons.title: Specialized clues can rescue ambiguous short words
lessons.body: A board made of short clues often needs one technical term to reveal the true category.

lessons.title: Common words may hide trade vocabulary
lessons.body: Band, Chain, Hack, and Jig all live outside the workshop too, which is why the saw category stays hidden longer than expected.

lessons.title: The most specific clue often deserves extra weight
lessons.body: Coping is not the most common everyday word on the board, but that is exactly why it confirms the tool family so well.
